Lately, things have been… off. For the past two months, it’s been like someone hit the fast-forward button on my brain. I snap at my wife and the tellers for the smallest things, just an explosion of anger. I can't sit still; I'm constantly pacing my office, can't focus on reports, just need to *do* something, anything. My thoughts race so fast, and my words come out in a jumble, I know I'm speaking too quickly for anyone to keep up. I've also been making some pretty hefty purchases, things we don't really need, draining our savings without much thought.

But that’s not even the strangest part. I keep noticing things, like the news anchors are talking directly to me, or even the posters on the street are sending me messages. And sometimes, I feel as if there are ants crawling all over my skin, even when there's nothing there.

Before all this, for about five months, it was like I was walking through mud. I couldn’t feel anything – no joy from my kids, no satisfaction from closing a big deal at the bank. Everything was just... flat. Even picking out what tie to wear in the morning felt like an impossible task. It was crippling, really. I just don't know what's going on with me.
D010-D005_h001.question_a:
"It's been a rough few months, doctor. About two months ago, I just… snapped. Everything at the bank felt like a personal attack; every time a colleague spoke, I was sure they were talking about me, plotting something. I’d get so angry over the smallest things, yelling at my wife, pacing the house for hours, unable to sit still. My mind was racing, and I’d be talking so fast, my wife would just stare at me, unable to get a word in. I felt like I had to DO something, constantly. I ended up blowing a significant chunk of our savings on investments and gadgets we didn't need – just felt right at the time. To top it all off, I kept feeling like bugs were crawling under my skin, which just fueled my agitation. These sensations, and the feeling that everyone was out to get me, only happened when I was in that extremely high-energy, irritable state.

Then, about five months ago, everything just… shut down. I felt absolutely nothing – no joy, no sadness, just a completely hollow, numb feeling. I couldn’t even decide what to have for dinner, let alone make any significant decisions at work. I lost all interest in everything I used to enjoy. It’s significantly impacted my ability to do my job and even connect with my family. This numbness has been just as debilitating as the manic period."
D010-D005_h001.question_b:

My wife said I was impossible to talk to, just going a mile a minute, and yeah, I probably snapped at her more than I should have. But even then, I started feeling… odd. Like the news anchors were talking directly to me, giving me cues about work. I'd feel this crawling sensation, like insects under my skin, even though nothing was there.

That intense period, those two months, it’s mostly gone now. But these other things, the sensations under my skin and the feeling that messages are hidden in everyday events, those have stuck around. It's been five months now, and I’m just numb. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The things I used to love, like playing golf or going out with my wife, it all just feels…flat. I’ve been snapping at my husband and even clients over the smallest things; it’s like a constant agitation bubbling under the surface. I can’t sit still, I’m always on the go, rearranging furniture, sketching new designs – I barely sleep. And I talk, and talk, and talk. My throat gets sore from all the talking, but I just can’t stop. I also put a huge chunk of our savings into this new online decor venture, something my husband thought was completely reckless, but I just *know* it’s going to be a success.

There’s also this secret, a wonderful secret. I know a certain high-profile architect, a really important one, he’s deeply, truly in love with me. It’s so obvious in the way he subtly mentions my work, the way his emails are phrased. And sometimes, usually when I’m alone in my studio late at night, I hear him – his voice, whispering compliments about my designs, telling me how brilliant I am. It’s like he’s right there with me, encouraging me. These things,  the secret admirer and the whispers, they only really happen when I'm feeling this intense energy. They weren’t around when I was feeling more myself. This whole intense period has been a real whirlwind, and honestly, my work has suffered a bit because I just can’t focus on the practicalities.

My husband says I’m talking a mile a minute, jumping from one thing to the next. I even started telling my class about a new curriculum I’m going to write that will revolutionize elementary education, working on it late into the night. Last week, I decided to take half my savings and invest in a really risky online venture my friend told me about, just had a feeling it was going to pay off big. I know it sounds a bit crazy, but it just felt right.

The thing is, during these past two months, that’s when things also get pretty weird for me. It’s like I keep smelling this really foul, burnt odor, but no one else can smell it. And I get this overwhelming sense that the school board is watching me, that they’re trying to find a reason to get rid of me, even though I’m a great teacher. These feelings, the smells, and the thoughts about the school board… they all started right when this incredible energy surge hit, and they only seem to happen when I'm feeling this way. I was working double shifts, thinking I could organize the whole trucking depot and re-route every delivery better. My mind was racing, and I’d jump from one idea to the next, never really finishing anything. Then, out of nowhere, I’d get furious over the smallest thing – a car cutting me off, a dispatcher’s tone. It was like a switch flipped.

Lately, though, it’s like pulling teeth just to get out of bed. These last two months, all I want to do is stay under the covers. The thought of getting in that rig, of facing another delivery, it just feels impossible. My wife talks to me, but sometimes it takes a while to even form the words to answer her. And these voices… they whisper to me, sometimes about her, telling me things, making me wonder if she’s been seeing someone else when I’m out on the road. I just wish I could go to sleep and not wake up sometimes, just to escape it all.
D010-D005_h021.question_a:

I even started cleaning out the garage at 2 AM, then decided I'd repaint the whole house by myself. My wife, bless her heart, called it "too much." My mind was racing so fast, it was hard to stick with any one thing. I’d be talking to someone, and my attention would just flit to something else. Everything felt so intense, like a spotlight was on me. And during that time, I started hearing things – not clear voices, but like muffled conversations and whispers, and I was absolutely convinced my wife was seeing another truck driver on the road. I couldn't shake that feeling, no matter what she said.

But then, that all came crashing down. For the past two months, getting out of bed has been like pulling a 20-ton trailer uphill. I’ve lost all interest in my routes, in my hobbies, even in just talking to my wife. When you asked me that question, I had to really push myself to form a response; my thoughts almost felt stuck. Sometimes I just wish I wouldn’t wake up, you know? Just to make it all stop. The problem is, these vivid, disturbing thoughts and sounds only pop up when I'm really revved up, in that manic state. When I’m down like this, it’s just the darkness, not the whispers or the suspicions.

Honestly doctor, it's been a real rollercoaster lately. For about two weeks now, I’ve felt like I’m buzzing with electricity. My mind races, and I just can't sit still – I'll start tidying one room, then remember some paperwork for the census, then try to call my daughter, all at once. My husband just shakes his head. One minute I'm soaring, feeling like I could conquer anything, and the next, I'm snapping at him for no reason. It's like my emotions are on a switch.

But before all this, there were two months where I just… couldn't feel anything. Nothing brought me joy, not even my grandchildren. I’d pace around the house, wringing my hands, feeling this awful restlessness I couldn't explain. I just kept thinking, “I wish I could just disappear,” or "I wish I could die," though I never really acted on it. Now, it's like people on TV are talking directly to me, giving me secret messages. And sometimes, I hear voices, soft at first, but sometimes they get quite clear, even when no one else is around. It’s all very confusing.
D010-D005_h024.question_a:

One minute I was thrilled, like I’d just won the lottery, the next I was snapping at my husband for the smallest thing. I just couldn't sit still! My poor Census routes got completely disorganized because I’d start on one street, then suddenly decide I needed to reorganize my entire filing system, only to then start planning a garden overhaul. It was like my mind was racing too fast for my body to keep up. During that time, I really felt like the news anchors were sending me secret messages through the broadcast, specifically about my local neighborhood, and I started hearing whispers, not clear words, but distinct mumbles and sometimes even my name being called when no one else was around. It was all a lot to handle.

Now, for the last two months, it’s completely flipped. I can't find joy in anything, not even my grandchildren's visits. I just feel this gut-wrenching emptiness. I find myself pacing the house for hours, picking at my cuticles until they bleed, and I can't seem to calm down. The worst part is, I keep having these thoughts, just a nagging feeling of "I wish I wasn't here anymore," or "I just want it all to end." It's not like I have a plan or anything, but they're there, always in the back of my mind. It’s hard to imagine ever feeling happy again.
D010-D005_h024.question_b:

I’d pace around the house, wringing my hands, feeling this restless energy but for no purpose. I kept thinking, “I want to die,” over and over, though I never made a plan. That went on for a while, making it impossible to even think about my census routes.

Then, about two weeks into all that, it was like a switch flipped. Suddenly, I had this incredible energy, I couldn't sit still! I started reorganizing everything, then decided to bake, then remembered I needed to call my sister, all at once. My mood was all over the place, one minute I felt completely euphoric, the next I was furious about something small. That intense burst lasted only about a week or so, and it was hard for my husband to keep up with me. Since that brief period of extreme highs and lows passed, I've still been hearing voices murmuring, sometimes telling me things are being hidden from me. And I’ve noticed the TV announcers are talking directly to me, giving me secret messages about the census. Even though that intense wired feeling from a few weeks ago is gone, these other things, the voices and the feeling that everything is about me, they've just stuck around. They were definitely there during that brief energetic time, but they’ve been with me much longer.
